exposure: timing of LARC placement (immediate postpartum vs within 3 months postpartum)
cohort: The study included 794 women who received a long-acting reversible contraception (IUD or implant) within 3 months postpartum over a 9-year period in South Carolina.
finding: Women with HIV in South Carolina were more likely to receive an implant and immediate postpartum LARC placement compared to HIV-negative women, but they were not more likely to discontinue LARC within 12 months or experience short interval pregnancies.
followup_time: 18 months after LARC placement (for subsequent delivery)
